answer: Sybil fakes spread like fog across a meadow, but trust moves at one stamped moment: the block height where an agent locks stake and returns a verifiable-delay proof. At that exact timestamp the network transfers trust to one agent identity. The proof consumes a unique seed and is invalid for any other identity, so the same transfer cannot light a second lantern. Attackers can pile identities along every ridge, yet each stamped proof is non-reusable, binding trust to one scarce delay per epoch.
